info.description: Per-user codchi-server v1 contract. See v1/phases/00-contract-decisions.md.

ApiError.description: Typed API error. Serialized as an internally-tagged object with a stable `code` discriminator, e.g. `{"code":"machine_not_found","machine":"foo"}`.

oneOf.description: No machine with this id exists.
Another writer job holds this machine (P7 rule 2).
`create` rejected: the id is reserved by a terminal-failed create job that still has retained artifacts (R9 / Phase 5 JS-D3). The client can inspect or clear `job` to free the id.
No job with this id exists, or its metadata was pruned.
The job is past the point where cancellation is accepted (P7).
An operation that requires a finished job (e.g. `prepare_job_debug`, `delete_job_artifacts`) was called on a still-running job (Phase 5 JS-D2).
The job has no retained artifacts to debug or delete (Phase 5 JS-D2).
The store is unavailable, migrating, or needs repair (P7 rule 5).
A store repair/migration job is already running (P7).
The on-disk SQLite schema must be migrated before serving.
The client and server disagree on the API major version (Q5).
Implicit start blocked because declared secrets are unset (R5).
`get_secret` on a key that is declared but has no stored value (MS10), so the CLI can say "declared, set it" rather than "no such secret". Unknown keys are `Validation`, not this.
A request field failed validation (P4). `field` is the request field path (e.g. `id`, `source`, `target`).
Unexpected server-side failure.

Component.description: The subsystem a finding pertains to.

ConfigResolution.description: Typed output of `resolve_config` and the matching [`crate::dto::job::JobOutput`] variant.

nixpkgs_input_present.description: Whether the flake exposes a `nixpkgs` input that machines may follow.

ConfigurationStatus.description: Pure desired-versus-active configuration projection (Phase 4 MS11); replaces beta's `UpdateStatus`. Never stored — derived on every machine read. Update-availability ("a newer remote input exists") is deliberately **not** on this axis (MS11): it requires fetching remote inputs and is a future separate in-memory field.

oneOf.description: Only on the synthesized in-flight-create view (active_generation `None`).
Active generation's configuration snapshot equals the desired config.
Desired config differs from the active generation's snapshot.

CreateMachineRequest.description: Create a new machine (job). All inputs are supplied up front; the job runs to success or fails (R9).

keep_on_fail.description: On failure, retain the failed **create job**'s artifacts (its diagnostic workspace + partial platform resources) for introspection, reserving the machine id until cleared (R9/MS1 — there is no durable machine row to retain). Defaults to `false` (tear down completely).

DoctorOpts.description: Options for the `doctor` read and `doctor_scan` job.

machine.description: Restrict to a single machine, if set.

DuplicateMachineRequest.description: Duplicate an existing machine into a new, independent one (job, MS13). The source is the `{id}` path segment of `POST /machines/{id}/duplicate`; only the new name travels in the body. Not a rename: the source is untouched and the result has its own fresh generation history. The filesystem copy and the source-stopped requirement are Phase 7.

Duplicated.description: Typed success payload of a `duplicate` job (MS13): the new machine's first generation.

Event.description:
One event on a job stream. Adding variants is non-breaking; renaming or removing one is breaking (Q5).

Per R8 these split across persistence tiers: `Progress` is a throttled in-memory aggregate (never persisted per-delta); the raw build firehose is live-only `Log` (topic `build`) and is not replayed; `Phase`, `StateChange`, `NixBuild`, `HealthFinding`, and `Log` for nix `Msg{Error,Warn}` / eval errors are the durable, replayable tier.

EventSeq.description: Per-job monotonic event sequence number (Q2). Wire-stable `u64`.

EventStreamOpts.description:
Query options for `stream_job_events` and `stream_logs` (Q2, R14).

R14 dropped `since_seq` resume: streams are followed over a per-user Unix socket that doesn't transiently reconnect, so the only knobs are how much history to backfill on attach (`tail`) and whether to keep following (`follow`). `seq` still orders the NDJSON and anchors `tail`'s "last N".

follow.description: Keep streaming after the current tail. Default `true`.

tail.description: Backfill the last N events before following. Default [`DEFAULT_TAIL`].

ExecPlan.description: Everything a client needs to attach an exec session once the machine is ready.

cwd.description: Working directory inside the machine, if one was resolved.

target.description: Platform resource the client execs into (Podman container / WSL distro name, derived from the machine id).

Finding.description: A single health finding produced by the reconciler or a `doctor_scan`.

auto_fixable.description: `true` only if repair cannot touch user data or rewrite `flake.lock`.

FindingCode.description:
Stable machine-readable identity of a health finding.

Each variant declares its wire string explicitly so Rust refactors cannot silently change the contract.

FindingsSummary.description: Counts of active findings by severity. Lets the tray render a badge without a `doctor` call.

GenerationStatus.description: Lifecycle of a generation. Shared by machine and store generations.

oneOf.description: Currently activated.
Built and retained, not active.
Pinned against garbage collection.
Tombstoned; retained only for history.

GenerationView.description: One machine generation (a built + activatable system).

source_job.description: The job that produced this generation.

JobFilter.description: Query filter for `list_jobs` (R11). All fields optional; omitted ⇒ no constraint. Fields flatten to query parameters.

machine.description: Restrict to jobs acting on this specific machine.

subject.description: Restrict to jobs whose subject is of this kind.

JobKind.description: What a job does. No `Start`/`Stop`/`Restart` (R6); no `Reconcile` (P6).

oneOf.description: R3: read-only flake fetch+eval → [`crate::dto::config::ConfigResolution`].
R7: ensure store+machine running, session, env → [`ExecPlan`].
R11: bring up the store container (a `Store`-subject job).
R11: bounded store recovery (a `Store`-subject job).

JobOutput.description:
Type-erased terminal success output, one variant per producing [`JobKind`]. Each variant wraps the same payload type the corresponding typed [`JobView<O>`] carries, so a `JobView<Rebuilt>` and a type-erased [`JobView`] of the same job describe the same data. Adding a variant is additive (Q5). A `None` `JobView.output` is valid for kinds with no payload (e.g. `delete`, `activate_generation`).

This is the output type of the kind-erased [`crate::service::CodchiService::get_job`]; the kind-specific job methods return a narrowed [`JobView<O>`] instead.

Typed success payload of a `garbage_collect` job: bytes freed in the store.

JobView_for_ConfigResolution.description:
The canonical view of a job, generic over its typed success output `O`.

A terminal job is exactly one of: `Failed` with `error: Some(_)`, or `Succeeded` with `output` set — or `output: None` for kinds with no output (R1). The type parameter makes the success payload visible at the call site: kind-specific methods return e.g. `JobView<Rebuilt>` or `JobView<()>` (no output), while the kind-erased [`crate::service::CodchiService::get_job`] returns the default `JobView` = `JobView<JobOutput>`.

last_event_seq.description: Highest event sequence emitted so far.

output.description: `Some` iff terminal `Succeeded` for kinds that produce output (R1/R2).

subject.description: The log source this job acts on (R11). Machine-less operations (`resolve_config`, `doctor_*`, `migration`) are `Server`-subject; store operations are `Store`-subject.

Lifecycle.description:
Server-derived display rollup of where a machine is in its lifecycle (R10). Computed once from `active_generation` + `run_status` so every client renders the same label without re-deriving the orthogonal axes; never stored.

Derivation (total):

```text active_generation is None   => Creating     (synthesized in-flight create, MS1) run_status is None          => Reconciling  (born, no observation yet) run_status is Some(Absent)  => Absent       (container removed out-of-band) run_status is Some(Stopped) => Stopped run_status is Some(Running) => Running ```

oneOf.description: Synthesized in-flight-create view: the create job is running and no durable machine row exists yet (`active_generation == None`, MS1).
Born machine with no reconciler observation yet (e.g. just after daemon restart, or an initial probe in flight).
Container confirmed removed out-of-band (`run_status == Some(Absent)`).

LockInputChange.description: One changed flake input in an `update` job's lock diff.

new_rev.description: New locked revision, if the input still exists after.

old_rev.description: Previous locked revision, if the input existed before.

LogSource.description:
A long-lived log-emitting entity (R11).

Adjacently tagged on the wire — `{"type":"server"}`, `{"type":"store"}`, `{"type":"machine","id":"foo"}` — because the `Machine` variant wraps a transparent-string newtype, which serde cannot internally tag.

oneOf.description: The `codchi-server` daemon itself.
The store container.
A machine container.

LogSourceKind.description: The id-less kind of a [`LogSource`], used to filter `list_jobs`.

MachineDetail.description: The detail view of a machine.

MachineView.description: The list view of a machine. Returned from the daemon-maintained snapshot; read endpoints must not probe synchronously (P6).

active_generation.description: `None` ⇒ synthesized in-flight-create view only; no durable machine row is ever `None` (R9/MS1 — a machine is born at its first generation commit).

busy_with.description: The in-flight job owning this machine, if any.

lifecycle.description: Server-derived lifecycle rollup for display (R10) — folds `run_status` + `active_generation` into one label.

run_status.description: Raw platform-container observation; `None` until the reconciler reports one (MS2). For the display rollup use `lifecycle`.

state_version.description: Per-machine **state**-format version for state migration (MS12/MS15): `0` for beta-migrated machines, `>= 1` otherwise. This is the per-machine state version (the renamed `schema_version` idea), distinct from the global DB schema version (`PRAGMA user_version`).

MigrationMachinePlan.description: What migrating one beta machine would do.

blockers.description: Why this machine cannot be migrated as-is (P4 dry-run flags), if any. Empty ⇒ migratable.

source_name.description: Beta machine name as found on disk.

MigrationPlan.description: A pure plan/read view of a beta → v1 migration.

beta_detected.description: Whether a beta installation was detected at all.

MigrationSummary.description: Result summary of a completed migration.

ModuleSpec.description: A single module a machine pulls in (Phase 4 MS8). The complete canonical Codchi flake URL — including its `#attr` module attribute path — is the module's whole durable identity; modules have **no** user-visible name (beta's mutable map-key handles are not domain identity). The canonical URL form and its normalizer are tracked in `v1/todo/flake-url-canonical-form.md` and locked with the Phase-6 generated-`flake.nix` normalizer.

is_nixpkgs_source.description: Whether this module supplies the machine's `nixpkgs` input (beta `nixpkgs_from`). At most one module per machine may set this (MS8).

url.description: Canonical Codchi flake URL including the module attribute path. The whole durable identity of the module (MS8).

PrepareExecRequest.description: Request to prepare an exec session into a machine. The target machine is the `{id}` path segment of `POST /machines/{id}/exec`; only the command body travels here.

command.description: Command + args to run. `None` requests an interactive login shell.

Rebuilt.description: Typed success payload of a `rebuild` job: the new active generation.

ResolveConfigRequest.description: Request to resolve a flake url into its available modules.

url.description: Flake url to fetch and evaluate (codchi flake-url form, the `#attr` part may be omitted — resolution discovers the available attrs).

RunStatus.description: Raw platform-container observation, from the in-memory reconciler snapshot (P6, Phase 4 MS2): the status of the realized container *itself*. Carried as `Option<RunStatus>` on `MachineView`, where `None` means the reconciler has not reported an observation yet — surfaced to users as `Lifecycle::Reconciling`, not a `RunStatus` variant. Integrity failures are represented as `findings`, not a runtime `Failed` state. The reconciler that produces these is Phase 5/7; SQLite never stores them (MS2).

oneOf.description: The container is confirmed gone. A machine is born only at a successful platform install (MS1), so the only way a born machine observes `Absent` is its container being removed out-of-band (e.g. `podman rm`).

SchemaStatus.description: SQLite schema status. The daemon migrates synchronously before it serves, so there is no observable mid-migration state to report (see `v1/phases/03-sqlite-foundation.md`, DB8); `current` and `required` are equal in steady state and differ only momentarily during the (un-served) startup migration.

SecretKey.description: A secret key as surfaced by `list_secrets` — the union of {active-generation declared keys} ∪ {keys with a stored value} (MS10). Values are never carried on this type.

description.description: Human-readable description: from the active generation's declaration for `Declared` keys, or the value row's stored `description` — refreshed on every config eval, frozen once the key drops out — for `Obsolete` ones (MS10).

has_value.description: Whether a plaintext value is currently stored for this key.

status.description: Whether the key is still declared or a dangling obsolete value (MS10).

SecretStatus.description: Whether a secret key is still declared by the active generation, or a dangling value left behind after its declaration dropped out (Phase 4 MS10).

oneOf.description: Declared by the active generation's secret schema.
No longer declared, but a stored value survives (not projected into the machine env; surfaces a `secret.obsolete_value` finding).

ServerStatus.description: Server status (P5). `api_version` is also exposed as an HTTP response header on every call; this field is authoritative for consumers of this endpoint.

server_version.description: Build version of the running server.

startup_error.description: `Some` only when `lifecycle` indicates a recoverable failure.

SetModulesRequest.description: Write a machine's desired module set (sync). Marks `needs_rebuild`; does not auto-trigger a rebuild (Q4).

SetSecretRequest.description: Body for `set_secret` — the plaintext value (the key is in the path).

value.description: Plaintext secret value. Never logged; never placed on event streams.

Severity.description: Finding severity, ordered least → most severe.

StoreGenerationView.description: One store generation. Read-only in v1 (no activation endpoint); exposed for diagnostics and tray display.

StoreState.description: Store availability, fed by the 15 s store sentinel (P6), not a fresh probe.

Updated.description: Typed success payload of an `update` job: the new generation plus the `flake.lock` diff.
